speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes and if anyone else is there with you when it occurs? Also, do you ever scream or run around during these times?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night terrors.

Based on the history of an 8-year-old waking up frightened, yelling, and crying with no confusion afterward, this pattern is most consistent with night terrors (sleep terrors). Since she is easily consoled and retains normal alertness upon waking, this helps distinguish it from a nightmare. I will confirm the diagnosis based on these classic features.
